title: Adjoints and small localizations of presentable infinity categories
statement: Let $\mathcal C,\mathcal D$ be presentable infinity categories, meaning accessible infinity categories admitting all small colimits, with sizes fixed in nested universes as in [def-coef-complete-algebroid]. They admit all small limits. A functor $F:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ has a right adjoint if and only if it preserves small colimits. For any small set $S$ of arrows in $\mathcal C$, the full subcategory of objects $Z$ such that $\operatorname{Map}(B,Z)\to\operatorname{Map}(A,Z)$ is an equivalence for every $(A\to B)\in S$ is presentable and its inclusion has an accessible left adjoint. Its limits are computed in $\mathcal C$ and its colimits are obtained by applying that left adjoint to the colimits in $\mathcal C$. Adjunctions here are mapping-space adjunctions with coherent units, counits and triangle identities.
